The sender is an "allowed" rule (a look-alike domain is not ours), the link is a "lookup" (the sender decides where its links may go: the older plan's "match"), the request is an "allowed" rule with "odd_values" (the real IT reminder asks you to open the portal yourself), and the time is an "info" rule (a fake can come at any hour). The threat is the look-alike c0mpany-it.com and the request to type your password here, which repeat in bad logs.

rules.name: Sender
rules.text: Mail may come only from our own domains.
details: A look-alike (a zero for an o, an r and an n for an m) is not ours.
rules.why: A look-alike domain is made to be mistaken for ours.
rules.broken: comes from a domain that only looks like ours

rules.name: Link
rules.text: Each sender's links may go only to its own places.
rules.why: A link is only as good as where it goes, not what it says.
rules.broken: has a link that goes somewhere its sender should not send you

rules.name: Request
rules.text: A message may ask you to read, or to open the portal yourself.
details: A real notice never asks you to type a password into the message.
rules.why: Nobody real asks for a password, a code or a payment in a message.
rules.broken: asks for a password, a code or a payment

rules.name: Sent at
rules.text: The time alone decides nothing. A fake can arrive at any hour.
details: A real notice can come late, and a fake can come at lunch.
rules.why: Look at who sent it and where the link goes, not at the clock.
